bull.b: The shift from negative operating and free cash flow in 2021–2022 to sustained production gives Klaviyo internal funding for product investment and expansion. Strong cash generation also improves resilience and reduces reliance on external capital as the platform scales.

Growth in larger customers and the largest-ever multiproduct contract show that Klaviyo is moving further upmarket. Greater enterprise adoption can support larger recurring relationships, broaden customer reach, and create additional opportunities to expand product usage.

Gross margins in the 71%–76% range provide a strong economic foundation for a cloud software platform and leave room for operating leverage as revenue grows. Positive EBITDA and scale indicate the model can support reinvestment while progressing toward stronger profitability.

bear.b: Despite substantial revenue and cash generation, Klaviyo has only recently approached GAAP profitability. A very thin net margin leaves earnings vulnerable to expense growth, slower demand, or execution issues, and limits the current evidence of durable bottom-line operating leverage.

Text messaging is growing faster than the rest of the business, while carrier fees have increased, creating pressure on gross profit. Even with pricing actions, this mix dynamic can constrain margin expansion and require continued execution to preserve the platform’s economic profile.

Net revenue retention of 109% still reflects expansion, but the profile-enforcement comparison is expected to weigh on the metric across upcoming quarters. Lower retention expansion would make growth more dependent on new customer wins and could moderate the compounding effect of the installed base.
